question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

In October, / they will have lived / in San Francisco /for five years.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** "They will have lived", **is not grammatically incorrect on its own. However, the verb tense used in this segment may not be the most appropriate for the context of the sentence.
 
• The sentence is in the future perfect tense ("**they will have lived**"), which implies an action that will be completed before a certain point in the future. 
 
• However, the rest of the sentence ("**In October, they will have lived in San Francisco for five years**") suggests that the action of living in San Francisco for five years will be completed in October.
 
• To align the verb tense with the timing implied by the rest of the sentence, the more suitable option would be **"they will have been living"** instead of **"they will have lived."** 
 
• To align the verb tense with the timing implied by the rest of the sentence, the more suitable option would be "**they will have been living**" instead of **"they will have lived." **This change would reflect ongoing action up to the specified point in the future.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**option 4**'.

**Correct sentence**: In October, ***they will have been living ***in San Francisco for five years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 is inappropriate as there is no grammatical error.
